verbs.name: screen_record.preview_capability
verbs.description: Read whether this recorder build has an in-process native source-preview adapter and the only source-selection mode it admits. available/source_selection:exact accepts one current opaque monitor or window identity; available/source_selection:portal requires one fresh user-consented Linux system-picker selection. This is a capability fact, never a browser OS inference. It does not claim a source has been selected, permission is granted, or a frame arrived. Linux Portal preview owns a user-consented, ephemeral raw-frame session without GStreamer, ffmpeg, a child process, or synthetic pixels.
verbs.result: {state:'available',source_selection:'exact'|'portal'} or {state:'unsupported',prerequisite}. exact means only current opaque monitor/window ids may be used; portal means only {kind:'portal'} may be used and the user picks a source in the system dialog. This returns no source identity, screen name, native handle, frame, path, or permission claim.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_start
verbs.description: Start one bounded, process-local native source preview for exactly one opaque monitor or window identity from the current screen_record.doctor enumeration. Windows and macOS re-resolve that identity immediately; Linux accepts only Portal and opens a new user-consented, ephemeral PipeWire session. Every adapter retains only the latest bounded BMP in memory. A preview cannot start while a recording owns capture devices. Replacing a source stops/releases the predecessor first; no title, ordinal, native handle, region coordinates, file, restore token, or browser getDisplayMedia fallback is accepted.

monitor_id.description: Exact opaque identity copied unchanged from a current screen_record.doctor.monitors[].id row.

window_id.description: Exact opaque identity copied unchanged from a current screen_record.doctor.windows[].id row.

source.description: Exact source selector. Names, ordinals, geometry, primary-display fallbacks, and coordinates are not representable.

verbs.result: {action:'start',status:{state,recursion,has_frame,generation,lease_nonce?:string}}. state:'starting' means native admission only; ready requires a real delivered frame. lease_nonce is an opaque 128-bit per-Cut-server owner identity, present exactly while generation is active; pair it with generation for later lifecycle controls. It is neither authentication nor a native target/ticket. status intentionally omits the selected identity and private region.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_status
verbs.description: Read the current process-local native source-preview lifecycle. The owner polls only its already-admitted native mailbox; this never opens capture, starts a portal, reads a file, or returns the selected source. generation changes on every accepted Start/resume. lease_nonce is minted per Cut-server owner, changes after server restart, and must be paired with generation to reject delayed lifecycle controls.
verbs.result: {state:'idle'|'starting'|'ready'|'paused'|'hidden'|'permission_required'|'permission_denied'|'source_lost'|'unavailable'|'stopped',recursion:'none'|'detected'|'unavoidable',has_frame,generation|null,lease_nonce?:string,unavailable_reason?:string}. lease_nonce is opaque lowercase 32-hex and present exactly while generation is active; pair it with generation for lifecycle controls. ready is evidence of a retained real frame, never merely successful native startup. unavailable_reason is present only when the process cannot prove a prior native preview release; it states the required process-restart recovery.

verbs.name: screen_record.live_frame
verbs.description: Read one bounded real frame from the exact active recording's native source stream. This does not start a second capture, read an open media file, or control recording. The optional frame is cleared at each physical checkpoint rollover and at Stop or failure. State and separate controller-exclusion/recursion facts describe whether returned pixels may include the Cut window; backend policy may refuse preview independently.
verbs.result: {capture_id,state:'awaiting_source'|'awaiting_frame'|'ready'|'stale'|'unavailable'|'terminal',reason:string|null,generation:number,frame_age_ms:number|null,last_sample_cost_ms:number|null,max_sample_cost_ms:number,frame:null|{mime:'image/bmp',bytes:1..4194304,generation,captured_at_ms,base64}}. A frame belongs only to the returned capture_id and physical native generation; stale is a real retained frame older than five seconds. Preview failure never changes recording output.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_frame
verbs.description: Read the latest real native source-preview frame and lifecycle snapshot under one owner lock. It returns only a BMP data payload retained in memory by the active generation; no URL, path, image file, screenshot artifact, source identity, title, native handle, or synthetic frame exists. The encoded BMP is capped at 4 MiB before base64 encoding; frame:null is an honest no-frame result.
verbs.result: {status:{state,recursion,has_frame,generation,lease_nonce?:string},frame:null|{mime:'image/bmp',bytes:1..4194304,generation,captured_at_ms,base64}}. status.lease_nonce is paired with its active generation for lifecycle controls. frame.generation is bound to the returned bytes; a source replacement cannot mix old pixels with a new generation.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_pause
verbs.description: Pause the current native source preview only when expected_generation and expected_lease_nonce identify its active process-local lease, then synchronously release its native session and retained frame. resume reopens the exact remembered opaque source with a new generation. A stale generation or nonce is rejected without changing a newer or restarted-server preview. This does not pause a recording and has no filesystem or process side effect.

expected_generation.description: The exact active generation returned by preview_start, preview_status, or preview_frame.

expected_lease_nonce.description: The exact opaque lease_nonce returned with that active generation. It changes after Cut-server restart and is not an auth token or native target.

verbs.result: {action:'pause',status:{state,recursion,has_frame,generation,lease_nonce?:string}}. While paused, lease_nonce remains paired with generation for the later resume, hide, or stop control. A no-op pause reports the truthful existing lifecycle state.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_resume
verbs.description: Resume only the paused native source preview identified by expected_generation and expected_lease_nonce. A successful native re-open reports starting until a real callback frame arrives; it always advances generation before any frame can be accepted. A stale generation or nonce is rejected without changing a newer or restarted-server preview. This does not resume a recording and cannot recreate a released/hidden preview without a new preview_start.

expected_generation.description: The exact paused generation returned by preview_start or preview_status.

expected_lease_nonce.description: The exact opaque lease_nonce returned with that active generation.

verbs.result: {action:'resume',status:{state,recursion,has_frame,generation,lease_nonce?:string}}. The advanced generation carries the same active owner nonce for later lifecycle controls.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_hide
verbs.description: Hide the native source preview only when expected_generation and expected_lease_nonce identify its active process-local lease. It synchronously releases the native session and pixels if present, then reports hidden without auto-resuming capture. A stale generation or nonce is rejected without changing a newer or restarted-server preview. It does not alter a recording.

expected_generation.description: The exact active generation returned by preview_start, preview_status, or preview_frame.

expected_lease_nonce.description: The exact opaque lease_nonce returned with that active generation.

verbs.name: screen_record.preview_stop
verbs.description: Stop the native source preview only when expected_generation and expected_lease_nonce identify its active process-local lease. It synchronously releases the native session, latest frame, remembered source, and private region before returning stopped. A stale generation or nonce is rejected without changing a newer or restarted-server preview. screen_record.start atomically reserves ordinary capture before its internal preview release.

expected_generation.description: The exact active generation returned by preview_start, preview_status, or preview_frame.

expected_lease_nonce.description: The exact opaque lease_nonce returned with that active generation.
